correctness.rationale: Exact observed-residue and forcing characterization proves success iff at most one row or at most one column is initially empty, for all \(m,n\ge2\). Finite polynomial follows by two-dimensional inclusion-exclusion, with exact minimum counts. Mixed falling factorial moments are computed exactly for both Bernoulli and hypergeometric sensor sampling; method of moments proves independent Poisson limits, while binomial concentration and negative correlation treat infinite aspect crossover. A direct adjacency-based standalone checker exhaustively validates eight small boards, every coefficient, and rectangular exact moment identities. Finite checks are not offered as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The directly published rook-graph scalar power-domination minimum does not mathematically determine the finite all-sensor-set enumerator or the Bernoulli/fixed-budget Poisson crossover. Accessible full arXiv texts and targeted public-literature queries revealed no equal or dominating phase-diagram statement. The result is assessed as original relative to identified work, with material incomplete-access and indexing risks explicitly retained.
residual_risks: The full original Soh–Koh 2014 paper was inaccessible; its visible scalar result is not the entire contents.
The 2008 publisher article full text was not retrieved; its accessible abstract covers different products.
Possible unindexed earlier formulation in occupancy, phasor-measurement reliability, line-graph or Hamming-graph terminology; negative search results do not certify global novelty.

value.rationale: Power domination is a motivated monitoring/optimization invariant. Random placement requires a genuinely larger \(n\log n\) budget than the known optimal \(n-1\) placement; the near-square excess \(n/\log n\) is the nontrivial critical shape scale at which two occupancy failure channels transition to one. Exact polynomial coefficients supply finite reliability for every board and both sampling models. This shape sensitivity and sampling transition are not consequences of the scalar minimum alone and give a meaningful family-level result.
